Cliffside Park Municipal Court is the courthouse in Bergen County, New Jersey. It is situated in the municipal complex. It has jurisdiction over criminal, city ordinance violation, and DWI, traffic and vehicle matters. Regular court sessions were held every Thursday at 5:00 pm via zoom or in the court, while special DWI sessions were held every Tuesday. The court handles approximately 65 complaints of disorderly persons and over 200 traffic citations and DWI charges each month. Searching with file names is also available on the website.

How to search for the case record?

Cliffside Park Municipal Court records are available online and in the county clerk's offices. They can be found online by using the following ways:

  • Searching by name
  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by address
  • Searching by phone
  • Searching by email

Some recorded information about cases is not available online because they are lawfully confidential. These types of information are only available at the county court office. They can be obtained by giving an Open Public Records Request. Personal information is only given to the person involved in the case or to the police or investigation agency. For more information about the public records, call or mail the court.

The traffic court handles which types of cases?

Cliffside Park Municipal Traffic Court handles cases of traffic and vehicle violations. The violation includes speeding, accidents, using cell phones while driving, failing to follow a traffic signal or traffic control device, driving with a suspended or no license, leaving the scene of the accident, and driving recklessly. Your driving license and driving privileges will be suspended if you do not pay the fine on time. You cannot request your license renewal until the court approves. You need to hire a professional traffic ticket defense attorney if you receive a traffic ticket.

The criminal court handles which types of cases?

Cliffside Park Municipal Criminal Court handles cases of crimes, murder, drug usage, theft, assault or any other serious crimes. You can enter a plea of guilty or not guilty in these cases. Severe crime cases will result in a lot of fines and arrest warrants. You must hire a professional criminal defense attorney if you are involved in these cases.

How to send a plea in cases?

Cliffside Park Municipal Court can be sent through the mail. A form is available on the website. Two types of plea can be written and sent to court. The types are:

Plea of Guilty

If you are guilty or want to request a defensive driving or deferred disposition, you must tick the plea of guilty section and then write a note on your act or guilt. The court will respond to the response and the fine you had to pay. After taking the course, your cases can be removed from the records.

Plea of Not Guilty

If you do not feel guilty, tick the plea of a not guilty section of traffic or non-traffic cases, write a note on your defense with some proof and send it to the court. The court will give you a schedule, and you must appear in court on the program. You cannot request a defensive driving or deferred disposition in this case.

At the end of the form, write the date and your signature and mail it or go to the court in person.

How to make payments?

Cliffside Park Municipal Court traffic ticket and fines payment can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the counter. Convenience and other charges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card. Payment plans are also available by this court.

Online

A person can pay online using the New Jersey online payment link: http://www.njmcdirect.com/. Enter the ticket or citation number and pay the fine. Service fees will be applied in this method.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address. The address is 525 Palisade Ave, Cliffside Park, NJ 07010, United States. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted.

How to get a marriage license?

Cliffside Park Municipal Court's marriage license is obtained from the clerk's office and given by the health department of the municipal complex. The fee for a marriage license is $28. The couple's age must be 18+. If someone is under 18, written consent from parents, guardians, and the judge is mandatory. To get the certification, the couple had to submit a marriage form with an original sealed birth certificate issued by the state, social security number, and photo ids like a driver's license, Passport, or anything that could prove their identity. The application form is available at the clerk's office. If this is anyone's second marriage, a divorce paper or spouse death certificate must be required at the time of registration. You must bring a witness of 18+ when applying for the license.

What are the duties of the clerk?

Cliffside Park Municipal Court clerk's duty is to maintain each case file and receive and handle payment and fines. He is the custodian of the municipal seal. The clerk's office is the center of town business and the primary source of information regarding the town. They are responsible for the maintenance of all Official Town Records and the issuance of various licenses. They are an agent of licensing and custodians of the town records. They provide marriage licenses, birth and death certificates, permits, etc. The clerk is the governing body's secretary, the chief administrative officer of all the elections held in the municipality and the chief registrar of the voter.

FAQ:

Who collects fines for traffic tickets?

The violation Bureau collects fines for traffic Tickets.

I want some information regarding the marriage license; how can I get the information?

Call the municipal complex health department for marriage license information.

Phone: (201) 313-2042

What is an ODR Program?

Cliffside Park Municipal Court offers an Online Dispute Resolution Program that allows the court user to argue a charge and provide evidence to the prosecutor of the municipality online.

Can I take an online hearing of my case?

Yes, online hearings are available through the zoom application.

How can I request a zoom hearing?

Cliffside Park Municipal Court, zoom hearing requests can be made by mailing to court@cliffsideparknj.gov.
